title: Final exam: strings and multi-key sorting
overview: The final exam checks string scanning (replace a pattern, find an exact word) and array-of-object skills (mirror-swap a field, sort with two or three keys). Each program here is a clean pattern worth remembering.

concepts.explain: At each position, check if the pattern starts there; if yes, output a marker and jump past it.
Build words between spaces and remember to check the last word after the loop.
Swap element i with element n-1-i for i < n/2.
Compare key 1; if equal key 2; if equal key 3.

files.title: Final Q1: Replace a word with #
files.what: Walks through S; wherever X starts, it adds `#` and jumps past X, otherwise it copies one character.
steps: `matching_location(s1, s2, index)` checks that X fits and every character matches.
No match: append the character and move 1.
Store results and print them at the end.
files.output_note: `rahimisagoodguy good` gives `rahimisa#guy`. `aaaa aa` gives `##` - matches don't overlap because the scan jumps past each one.
files.watch_out: `matching_location` takes both strings by value, copying them on every call; `const string&` would be faster.

check.q: Why does `aaaa` with X = `aa` give `##` and not `###`?
check.a: After a match the scan skips the whole X, so matches never overlap.

files.title: Final Q2: Find Jessica
files.what: Builds each word character by character and checks for an exact `Jessica`.
steps: At a space, check `word == "Jessica"`, then reset `word`.
After the loop, check the last word too.
files.output_note: Prints `YES`: `Jessicarvai` doesn't count, but the last word `Jessica` does - found by the check after the loop.

check.q: Why is the check after the loop needed?
check.a: The last word is not followed by a space, so it would never be checked inside the loop.

files.title: Final Q3: Swap sections in mirror order
files.what: Reads N students and swaps the section of student i with the section of student N-1-i, leaving the other fields in place.
steps: Print all students in the original order.
files.input:
4
Rahim 7 A 101
Karim 8 B 102
Sakib 9 C 103
Tamim 10 D 104
files.input_note: N, then N lines `name class section id`.
files.output_note: Names, classes and ids stay; sections are reversed: A B C D becomes D C B A.
files.watch_out: The comment at the top is a copy of the Replace Word statement and does not describe this program.

check.q: What happens to the middle student when N is odd?
check.a: Its section stays the same, because the loop stops before it.

files.title: Final Q4: Sort by total marks
files.what: Sorts students by math + English (high to low); equal totals go by smaller id.
steps: Read all six fields per student.
On equal totals it returns `l.id < r.id`.
files.input:
4
asif 9 A 3 80 70
rina 8 B 1 90 60
joy 10 C 2 75 90
moni 7 D 4 95 70
files.input_note: N, then N lines `name class section id math english`.
files.output_note: joy and moni both have 165 (ids 2 and 4), then rina and asif both have 150 (ids 1 and 3).

check.q: How would you avoid writing the sum twice?
check.a: Store `int tl = l.math_marks + l.eng_marks` (and the same for `r`) at the top of the comparator.

files.title: Final Q5: Sort It Again (three keys)
files.what: Sorts by English marks descending, then math marks descending, then id ascending.
steps: If still equal, the smaller `id` comes first.
files.input:
6
akib 2 R 1001 32 53
rakib 1 E 1002 94 88
sakib 8 M 1003 34 88
bokib 3 Q 1004 93 58
jessica 4 F 1005 94 88
noname 8 R 1006 17 61
files.input_note: N, then N lines `name class section id math english`.
files.output_note: Matches the second sample from the statement: rakib and jessica tie on 94/88, so id 1002 comes before 1005.
files.watch_out: `id` can be up to 10^9, which still fits in an `int`.

check.q: With three keys, when is the id compared?
check.a: Only when both English and math marks are equal.

recap: Always handle the last word after a split-by-space loop.
Multi-key sorting: check each key in order, only moving on when equal.

check_yourself.q: Write the three-key comparator using `!=` checks.
check_yourself.a: `if (l.e != r.e) return l.e > r.e; if (l.m != r.m) return l.m > r.m; return l.id < r.id;`

check_yourself.q: How could you find an exact word in a line more simply?
check_yourself.a: Split the line with `stringstream` and compare each word with `==`.

check_yourself.q: In Q1, what does `matching_location` return when X doesn't fit before the end?
